title: {Funding Alert} Healthcare Startup Clinics On Cloud Secures $12.5 Mn in Series A Round
summary: Healthcare startup Clinics On Cloud secures 12.5 million dollars in Series A funding
detailed: Pune-based health-tech startup Clinics On Cloud has secured $12.5 million in a Series A funding round from Dubai-based investors through Model42, powered by Enlightened Minds Investments.

D2C home appliances brand Nuuk is reportedly in discussions to raise around Rs 100 crore (approximately $10.5 million) in a funding round led by Wipro Consumer Care Ventures and RPSG Capital Ventures, at an estimated valuation of Rs 500 crore (around $53 million).
Beyond Appliances recently raised Rs 110 crore in a Series B round, while Nester secured Rs 19 crore in pre-Series A funding in February 2026.
Mumbai-based quick-service restaurant (QSR) startup The Croffle Guys has secured Rs 14 crore in a funding round led by V3 Ventures.
sentences: Pune-based health-tech startup Clinics On Cloud has secured $12.5 million in a Series A funding round from Dubai-based investors through Model42, powered by Enlightened Minds Investments.

The company will utilise the newly raised capital to enhance its artificial intelligence (AI)-driven healthcare solutions, increase investment in research and development (R&D), and expand its network of connected microclinics.
The funding will also facilitate Clinics On Cloud's international growth strategy, with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) positioned as its central hub for global expansion.
The company is also looking to enter markets across Africa, the United States and Southeast Asia.

As part of its expansion plans, Clinics On Cloud aims to build strategic partnerships with healthcare providers, technology firms and organisations interested in setting up connected microclinics in different geographies.
Established in 2018 by Abhay Agarwal, Clinics On Cloud develops technology-based healthcare infrastructure with a focus on preventive care.
The startup has completed more than 3,500 deployments and facilitated over 12 million health screenings across eight countries.
The company initially entered the market with its Health ATMs and has since diversified its offerings to include Health Lounges, Box Clinics and Mobile Medical Units.

Its platform brings together preventive health screenings, AI-supported health insights and telemedicine services, enabling hospitals, pharmacies, healthcare entrepreneurs, corporates and government bodies to set up microclinics at workplaces, residential communities, shopping malls and underserved locations.
Clinics On Cloud's solutions have been adopted across government health centres, hospitals, corporate facilities and rural areas.
Its deployment network also extends to Indian defence establishments, including the Army, Navy and Border Security Force (BSF).
Looking ahead, the company intends to work with international healthcare innovators to incorporate artificial intelligence and advanced health screening technologies into its existing platform.

Essora Foods, a new-age beverage brand, has entered the Indian market with a portfolio of functional drinks targeting consumers seeking convenient beverage options across different everyday occasions.
Operating under the brand philosophy “Pure.
Lifestyle.”, the company aims to combine product quality, convenience, and varied flavours through its range of electrolyte and protein-based beverages.
The brand's initial portfolio includes four electrolyte variants: Tamarind, Shikanji with Chia Seeds, Mix Berries and Mango Chilli.
It also offers Protein Coffee and Protein Tea, catering to consumers with different flavour preferences and consumption habits.
Built around the concept of ‘Open.
Repeat.’, Essora Foods is focusing on convenient beverage formats suited to workdays, travel, workouts and everyday consumption.
The company said its product development approach centres on quality, ingredient awareness, transparency and accessibility.
Pooja Goyal, Founder and CEO, Essora Foods said, “Essora Foods was envisioned with the idea of making everyday beverage choices more convenient, enjoyable and accessible.
We want to create thoughtfully developed beverages that bring together quality, convenience and refreshing flavours for everyday consumption.
Our focus is on building a brand that values transparency, innovation and long-term relationships with consumers and business partners.

We believe there is significant potential in India's evolving beverage market, and we look forward to creating products that resonate with changing consumer preferences.”
The company's operating principles include five core values: Purity, Transparency, Sustainability, Community and Innovation.
It also plans to build consumer awareness through product sampling, creator collaborations, corporate associations, fitness communities, university partnerships and retail tie-ups.
Essora Foods intends to use influencer and creator partnerships to expand its digital presence across lifestyle, food, fitness and wellness audiences .
Corporate wellness programmes, institutional associations and distribution partnerships are also part of its market expansion plans.

Looking ahead, the brand plans to introduce new flavours and beverage formats while exploring packaging developments, consumer engagement initiatives and partnerships across retail and institutional channels.
“ Our ambition is to build a globally trusted beverage brand that stands for quality, accessibility and innovation ,” said Goyal.

D2C home appliances brand Nuuk is reportedly in discussions to raise around Rs 100 crore (approximately $10.5 million) in a funding round led by Wipro Consumer Care Ventures and RPSG Capital Ventures, at an estimated valuation of Rs 500 crore (around $53 million).

The proposed fundraise would exceed the company's $6.6 million Series A round, which it closed in August 2025 after securing a $2 million extension from existing investors Vertex Ventures SEA and Good Capital.
The final funding amount and valuation may change as discussions progress.
The companies involved had not responded to queries at the time of publication.
Founded in 2023 by Gazal Kalra, co-founder of logistics unicorn Rivigo, and Shalabh Gupta, former chief growth officer at Noise, Nuuk offers design-focused home and kitchen appliances.
Its portfolio includes cordless vacuum cleaners, fans, heaters, garment care products, air fryers, juicers, and mixer grinders.
The brand sells through its website, e-commerce platforms Amazon and Flipkart, and quick commerce platform Blinkit.
It has also expanded into offline retail, including a store in Delhi NCR.
The proposed investment follows the company's focus on product innovation, portfolio expansion, and strengthening its domestic supply chain.
In March 2025, Gupta said that around 20 percent of Nuuk's products were manufactured in India, with a target to increase this share to over 50 percent by the end of FY26.
The company designs its appliances in-house and works with third-party manufacturers.
Nuuk's operating revenue increased to Rs 16 crore in FY25 from Rs 31.8 lakh in FY24, its first full year of operations.
However, its net loss widened to Rs 39 lakh from Rs 7 lakh, while expenses rose to Rs 16.4 crore.
Nuuk competes with established appliance brands such as Philips and Bajaj, as well as newer players Atomberg and Lifelong.
The funding discussions come amid continued investment in the sector.
Beyond Appliances recently raised Rs 110 crore in a Series B round, while Nester secured Rs 19 crore in pre-Series A funding in February 2026.
Mumbai-based quick-service restaurant (QSR) startup The Croffle Guys has secured Rs 14 crore in a funding round led by V3 Ventures.
N.A.N Partners, the family office of Navin Agarwal, also participated in the investment round, which places the company's post-money valuation at Rs 100 crore.
The startup will deploy the fresh capital towards expanding its outlet network, with plans to establish more than 40 additional stores.
The expansion will be concentrated in Mumbai and Delhi, while the company will also explore selected locations in Pune, according to a press release.
Established in 2025 by Rahul Vohra, Annanya Agarwal, Amay Thakkar and Veer Pinto, The Croffle Guys operates in India's organised QSR market.
The brand specialises in croffles, a combination of croissants and waffles, and offers a menu featuring both sweet and savoury options.
Over the past year, the company has increased its store count from two to eight outlets.
It currently has an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 24 crore and is aiming to reach Rs 100 crore in annual revenue within the next 10 to 12 months.
The startup has reported close to threefold revenue growth during the last six months.
Its monthly revenue is currently around Rs 2 crore, and it aims to increase this to Rs 8 crore as it expands its operations and adds more outlets.
The Croffle Guys came into the national spotlight following its appearance on Shark Tank India, where it secured an investment deal worth Rs 2.5 crore at a company valuation of Rs 50 crore.
Meanwhile, V3 Ventures has backed various businesses across the food and consumer sectors, including Go Zero, Crème Castle, Dil Foods, Super You and Salad Days.
Through the latest funding, The Croffle Guys aims to strengthen its operations in existing markets and enter new locations.
Its expansion strategy is focused on building a wider retail presence and increasing its share in India's organised quick-service restaurant segment.
Gurugram-based premium grocery startup Solgram has secured over $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by DSG Consumer Partners and Saama Capital.
